rows.what_the_ink_shows: The interlinear insertion reads ‘R, le meilleur dénominateur possible’, with meilleur and possible visible (crops/14_scan064_L262_best_denominator.jpg). Its linked continuation at the upper paper edge reads ‘étant donné pr card Ker u’; the letters card and Ker are explicit, with no exponent wording (crops/14_scan064_L262_card_kernel.jpg). At the end of the page, puissance de is followed by a struck card and then uncancelled N (crops/14_scan064_L262_powers.jpg).
rows.note: Written claim: the best possible denominator is card Ker u. Intended mathematical correction supplied by the row: the least positive denominator is the exponent of the finite kernel group scheme; its cardinality is a possible denominator with the same prime support. Preserve the author's written claim. The example u=[2] on an elliptic curve in characteristic different from 2 has kernel order 4, whereas its rational inverse is (1/2)id and has least denominator 2. Thus card Ker u need not be the least denominator. The later power-of-N wording is retained. No other page was inspected.
rows.event_type: used and rechecked in this run
rows.event_outcome: Visually collated the full scan and three enlarged, contrast-raised crops, confirming the written claim that card Ker u is the best denominator. The limited counterexample argument is recorded as a separate targeted proof check.

additional_events.outcome: Checked only the denominator argument in the supplied elliptic [2] example: its rational inverse is (1/2)id, so 2 clears it; an integral inverse would make [2] an isomorphism, contrary to its nontrivial kernel. Given the supplied characteristic-not-2 kernel order 4, this refutes cardinality as the least denominator in that example. The general group-scheme exponent statement was not re-proved.
